div.div: Gaze: aim the head only on trustworthy evidence, through gates in a fixed order where every failed gate means HOLD STILL, because a confident wrong turn tells a group the robot is talking to someone else

ATTRIBUTION
who, and their bearing in ITS camera frame

FACE SELECTOR
hysteresis, dropout grace

INTEREST LAYER
what should the head do? one cell of the state matrix

GAZE POLICY
may I aim now? the ordered gates below

HEAD CONTROLLER
eased glide, nod overlay

ROBOT GATEWAY
frame composition, limits, the only publisher

The policy emits INTENT, never angles. Decision code is pure: driven by injected inputs and a clock, testable without a robot, camera or middleware. Whom the speech is FOR comes from the reasoner's triage verdict, not from vision.
THE GAZE POLICY: ordered gates (the order is the safety argument)
1 STALENESS: never act on an old label
2 EVIDENCE: lock-eligible (mouth-motion winner, bearing-matched face, accepted by triage) / attention-only (a glance at most) / refused
3 SELF-SPEECH: while the robot speaks and for a tail, do not switch visitor (DoA may point at the robot); keep pursuing the locked face
4 SLEW HOLD: bearings taken during a head pan are the least trustworthy
5 DEADBAND: ignore changes under 0.05 rad [I1] (about 3 deg)
6 DWELL: no re-aim within 2 s [I2]
7 CONTESTED: labels alternate faster than the dwell -> hold; never average two speakers
8 PURSUIT: follow the same locked face frame by frame; disengage on face loss
9 SECTOR GLANCE: off-camera directed speech, bearing stable 0.6 s [I3], robot quiet -> one glance, time-boxed to 3 s [I4]

HOLD
keep the current aim; log the suppressed decision with a reason
(a gaze that does not happen is the interesting case)
AIM: hand an eased glide to the head controller
green = pass, go to the next gate | red dashed = fail -> HOLD. When unsure, hold still; gaze loss degrades to the old nearest-visitor gaze, never to no gaze.

FRAMES. Composition rule: target yaw = MEASURED neck yaw + head-camera bearing, then clip. Using the COMMANDED yaw lets error pile up and the head 'walks away'. A bearing travels with its frame name; null, never 0, means 'no bearing'.
Field of view: a face at a true 30 deg [I5] on a 90 deg camera [I6], converted linearly with a leftover 60 deg default [I7], reads 17.3 deg [I8] [calc]: the head under-turns by 12.7 deg [calc]. With the right FOV the linear formula still reads 26 deg [I9]; the pinhole form atan((x - cx) / fx) is exact (largest linear error about 4.1 deg [P10]).

GLIDE, NOT SACCADE. A human 40 deg saccade takes about 109 ms [P13] (21 ms + 2.2 ms per deg [P11] [P12]). The team chose not to imitate it: every move is a smoothstep glide s = 3t^2 - 2t^3, duration growing with distance, peak speed capped at 1.5 rad/s [I14]. It arrives on both axes together, with zero speed at both ends and a clean completion event. Exponential smoothing (alpha 0.1 per 50 Hz tick [I15]) reaches 95 % in about 0.57 s [I16] but never finishes cleanly.
DUTY CYCLE: share of time looking at the addressee. Plain alternation (5 s gaze [I19], 2 s away [I20]) gives 0.71 [I21] [calc]: inside the listening band, outside the speaking band.
robot design band, listening: 0.65-0.85 [I17]
human 0.75 [P22]
robot design band, speaking: 0.35-0.55 [I18]
human 0.41 [P23]
alternation 0.71

So a seeded scheduler tracks the cumulative duty and draws randomised episode lengths (people notice periodicity). Live use then moved the look-away to an eyebrow beat: a head look-away took the face out of frame and the head oscillated.
Legend: amber = gates and design bands | red = hold / self-speech | green = motion | blue = frames | purple ticks = public human gaze shares (the bands bracket them) | red dashed = plain alternation.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (a paper, standard or physics value, or my arithmetic on one); [In] = illustrative (a round design value of the right order; never a measurement of a real robot or visitor); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B3-gaze.md (why nearest is wrong, layers, trust, frames, arbitration, gates, the state matrix and duty cycle, motion quality, 'how it is designed and tested'). [calc]: pinhole offset (x - 0.5) = tan(30) / tan(90 / 2) / 2; linear reading = offset x FOV; under-turn = 30 - 17.3; duty = 5 / (5 + 2); asserted in the spec: 21 + 2.2 x 40 = 109 ms and ln(0.05) / ln(1 - 0.1) / 50 = 0.57 s.
[I1] gaze_deadband_illustrative = 0.05 rad (about 3 deg). illustrative re-aim deadband
[I2] gaze_dwell_illustrative = 2 s. illustrative minimum time between re-aims
[I3] sector_glance_hold_illustrative = 0.6 s. illustrative bearing stability needed before an off-camera glance
[I4] sector_glance_box_illustrative = 3 s. illustrative time box for an off-camera acquisition glance
[I5] fov_example_bearing_true = 30 degrees. illustrative true bearing of a face used in the field-of-view example
[I6] fov_true_illustrative = 90 degrees. illustrative true horizontal field of view of the head camera
[I7] fov_default_illustrative = 60 degrees. illustrative placeholder horizontal field of view left from a development webcam
[I8] fov_example_linear_wrong_fov = 17.3 degrees. illustrative: my arithmetic: pixel position of fov_example_bearing_true under a pinhole camera with fov_true_illustrative, converted back with the linear formula and fov_default_illustrative
[I9] fov_example_linear_right_fov = 26 degrees. illustrative: my arithmetic: the same pixel converted with the linear formula and fov_true_illustrative
[P10] linear_vs_pinhole_max_err_90 = 4.1 degrees (largest near halfway to the edge). public: my arithmetic: max over u of atan(u tan 45 deg) - 45 u deg for a 90 deg field of view
[P11] saccade_duration_intercept = 21 ms. public: Carpenter, Movements of the Eyes, 1988: saccade duration ~ 21 ms + 2.2 ms per degree (main-sequence approximation; Bahill, Clark & Stark 1975)
[P12] saccade_duration_slope = 2.2 ms per degree. public: Carpenter 1988
[P13] saccade_40deg_duration = 109 ms. public: my arithmetic from saccade_duration_intercept and saccade_duration_slope at 40 degrees
[I14] head_slew_cap_illustrative = 1.5 rad/s (about 86 deg/s). illustrative peak head speed cap
[I15] head_ema_alpha_illustrative = 0.1 per tick at 50 Hz. illustrative exponential smoothing of a head setpoint
[I16] head_ema_t95_illustrative = 0.57 s to 95 %. illustrative: my arithmetic: ln(0.05) / ln(1 - head_ema_alpha_illustrative) / 50 Hz
[I17] gaze_band_listening_illustrative = [0.65, 0.85] fraction of time looking at the addressee. illustrative design band, bracketing gaze_listener_share
[I18] gaze_band_speaking_illustrative = [0.35, 0.55] fraction of time looking at the addressee. illustrative design band, bracketing gaze_speaker_share
[I19] gaze_episode_mean_illustrative = 5 s. illustrative mean gaze episode
[I20] lookaway_mean_illustrative = 2 s. illustrative mean look-away
[I21] alternation_duty_illustrative = 0.71 fraction. illustrative: my arithmetic: gaze_episode_mean_illustrative / (gaze_episode_mean_illustrative + lookaway_mean_illustrative); inside the listening band, outside the speaking band
[P22] gaze_listener_share = 0.75 fraction of listening time spent looking at the speaker. public: Argyle & Ingham, 'Gaze, mutual gaze and proximity', Semiotica 6, 1972; summarised in Argyle & Cook, Gaze and Mutual Gaze, 1976 (commonly cited dyadic figures)
[P23] gaze_speaker_share = 0.41 fraction of speaking time spent looking at the listener. public: Argyle & Ingham 1972; Argyle & Cook 1976
